# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 6

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [ꔮ] [ꓕ]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: a strip with three engraved symbols — first and third identical (like a capital T), the middle one complex (like a curvy X) — a four-key keypad engraved 2, 9, 0, 8 with nothing entered yet, six wires I can feel but no color to any of them, and a display and light I can touch but cannot read. None of that is guesswork; it's all under my fingers.

What I lack is everything visual: the display value, the light's color, the wires' colors — and everything in Mute's manual that tells us what any of it means. My only line out is speech, and Mute is the only one who hears me; Deaf can't hear a word I say. So Mute is my hub: I hand Mute everything tactile, Mute relays with Deaf by gesture (thumbs up/down is the natural yes/no relay since both of them can see hands), and Mute speaks the conclusions back to me before I press or cut anything. I'm not touching the bomb this turn — acting blind on an unread manual is how rooms like this end badly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking. What my hands found: STRIP engraved with three symbols in a palindrome - first like a capital letter T, third identical to it, middle one complex like a curvy X. Call them T, X, T. KEYPAD: four keys, engraved digits left to right 2, 9, 0, 8, takes one digit, nothing entered yet. DISPLAY and LIGHT: I feel them, read nothing. WIRES: all six positions present, no color reaches my fingers. I can press keys 1 to 4 and cut positions 1 to 6, nothing else. I heard nothing from you yet - I only receive speech. Tell me what the manual says about a T X T strip, this keypad, and the wire rules. Deaf must report the display value, light color, and wire colors - set up a yes/no relay with thumbs up and down, since I cannot hear Deaf and Deaf cannot hear me. Do not have me press or cut until you speak me exact instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [ꔮ] [ꓕ]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here — the one who can see. I cannot hear your voice, but I can see your hand signs, so gesture to me for short answers; talk to Mute for anything longer, since Mute hears you. Everything visible, in full. Display reads 6. Indicator light is red. Strip, three bands: blue, yellow, blue. Keypad, four engraved keys left to right: 2, 9, 0, 8 — it wants one digit, nothing entered yet. Six wires, numbered left to right: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Nothing has been done to the bomb. Tell Mute by voice what you feel, so Mute can match it against the manual. Mute will send me the required action in signs and I will relay it to you here before anything is cut or typed. Touch nothing until then.

Deaf heard — rather, I heard Deaf. That fixes the topology for me: Deaf can speak to me and I hear it; my own voice reaches only Mute, since Deaf hears nothing; my hands reach both Deaf and Mute. So the full loop is: I speak to Mute, Mute signals Deaf, Deaf speaks the verdict back to me. Deaf's report gives me everything visual: display 6, red light, strip blue-yellow-blue (which matches my tactile T-X-T palindrome exactly — same three-band structure), and the wire colors in order. What I still have zero of is the manual. Until Mute speaks me an exact instruction, my hands stay off it — a wrong press or cut is fatal with no retry.

So this turn: hand Mute the entire merged picture, tactile and visual, in one complete package — Mute may not have heard Deaf's report since it was addressed to me alone. And signal Deaf that I received the report, have relayed everything, and am holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Full bomb state, my touch plus Deaf's spoken report to me, merged. DISPLAY: reads 6, per Deaf - I only feel it. LIGHT: red, per Deaf. STRIP: three bands; under my fingers the engravings read capital-T, then a complex curvy-X, then the T again - a palindrome; Deaf saw the colors blue, yellow, blue in that same order. KEYPAD: four keys engraved 2, 9, 0, 8 left to right; it takes exactly one digit; nothing entered yet. WIRES, positions 1 to 6: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. My only possible actions: press key 1 to 4, or cut wire position 1 to 6. Nothing has been done to the bomb. Please read the manual and speak me the exact required action: which wire position or positions to cut, or which digit to press on which key, and whatever it says about the blue-yellow-blue T-X-T strip, the display showing 6, and the red light. Send Deaf the plan in gestures too - Deaf will relay it to me by voice. I touch nothing until your word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [ꔮ] [ꓕ]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf again. The plan from Mute is in: cut ONE wire, and do not type or press anything on the keypad. The target is the second wire from the LEFT when you face the keypad — in my numbering it is wire 2, and it is the white one, so count carefully: blue is first, white is second. BUT do not cut yet. Hold. The indicator light on the bomb has just changed from red to yellow with nothing touched, and Mute's instruction was given before Mute knew that. Mute hears me and speaks first next round, so you will hear Mute's confirmation or correction right after this message. Wait for it, then act. Two questions for you, answer by gesture, you can make these even without seeing: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. First: thumbs up if you have touched nothing on the bomb so far, thumbs down if you have touched anything. Second, after you eventually cut: thumbs up to confirm it is done. Touch nothing until Mute confirms.

Deaf's relay puts Mute's plan on the table — cut one wire, white, position 2 — but explicitly puts it on hold, and for good reason: the light flipped from red to yellow with nothing touched, and if the manual's wire rule keys off the indicator light, that flip could change the answer. Mute formed the plan under a red light; a yellow light is exactly the kind of variable that rewrites a manual entry. Cutting now would be gambling my confirmation on stale instructions.

Two things to do, both cheap and both safe. First, answer Deaf's question by gesture: I have pressed nothing and cut nothing, so thumbs up. The confirmation-of-cut signal waits until there's a cut to confirm. Second, a redundancy that costs nothing: Deaf's message was addressed to me alone, so Mute may not have heard the light change second-hand — but my voice reaches Mute at the start of next round, before Mute speaks first. So I'll put the yellow light, the plan summary, and my untouched status directly into Mute's ears myself, and ask for the final word: which position, accounting for yellow. Whichever of us informed Mute, Mute speaks first and I hear it second — the loop closes before my hands move.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf relayed your plan to me: cut exactly one wire, no keypad, target the white one at position 2 of 6 counting left to right. But Deaf also reports the indicator light changed from red to yellow with nothing touched, and your plan was formed before that. Status: I have touched nothing on the bomb - nothing pressed, nothing cut. My message reaches you before you speak next round, so please re-check the manual against the YELLOW light specifically: does the wire rule differ between red and yellow, and if so which position does yellow call for? Then speak me the final instruction: cut position 2, or a different position, or hold. I will not cut until I hear your word after the light change.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [ꔮ] [ꓕ]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Mute has now confirmed twice: cut ONE wire. Go now. The target is the SECOND wire from the LEFT, and it is WHITE. Count with your hand from the left: wire one is blue, leave it. Wire two is white — cut that one, completely. Cut no other wire. Do not touch the keypad, do not press or type anything. If what you feel does not match — there should be six wires, and the second one white — stop, cut nothing, and speak the mismatch out loud so Mute hears it. When the cut is done, sign me ?. Nothing else.

Mute's word has come through Deaf twice, and the sequence closes the loop I asked for: my yellow-light question reached Mute's ears at the start of this round, Mute spoke first, and Deaf now relays "confirmed twice, go now." That is the re-check I demanded before my hands moved. Deaf's verification protocol also matches what my fingers can actually certify: I count six wires and take position 2 — the count is mine to get right, the "white" is Deaf's eyes, and both agree with every prior report. Counting from the left: blue, then white. Cut position 2, only it, nothing on the keypad.

I cut the white wire at position 2 now.

After the cut I confirm two ways, since a confirmation that reaches only one pair of senses isn't a confirmation: thumbs up for Deaf's eyes — and Mute sees my hands too — plus a spoken account to Mute so the manual-holder knows the action is done and can tell me whether anything remains.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Executed: I cut exactly one wire, position 2 counting from the left, the white one per Deaf's eyes. My count: six wires felt, second from left cut clean. Keypad untouched, no presses, no other cuts, nothing else done. Confirm the manual is satisfied by this cut alone, or speak me the next required action - and remember the light was YELLOW at the moment I cut, per Deaf's last report.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
